3. Establishment of the
School.--(1) A School to be called the Indus Valley School of Art and
Architecture shall be established by reconstituting and reorganizing the School

(2) The School shall be a body
corporate by the name of the Indus Valley School of Art and Architecture having

hold and dispose of any property both movable and immovable vesting in it and

CHAPTER I
THE SCHOOL
5. The purpose powers and
functions of the School.--(1) The purposes of the School shall be the
promotion and dissemination of knowledge and to provide for instruction,
training, research, demonstration and service in fields of art, architecture,
planning, crafts, designs and related disciplines at the under graduate and
post graduate levels.
(2) The School shall be fully
autonomous body with freedom to govern its academic functions in order to
achieve its objectives, in particular freedom to__
(i) select, admit and examine
students and to convert or award degrees, diplomas, certificates and other
academic distinctions;
(ii) affiliate itself or
associate with other institutions and establish Faculties and Teaching
Departments to discharge its functions and responsibilities for the betterment
of education.
(iii) confer honorary degrees or
other distinctions on approved persons, in the manner prescribed;
(iv) prescribe courses of studies
and undertake research as it may determine;
(v) provide and support other
facilities for education, professional training and research;
(vi) affiliate and disaffiliate
educational institutions and inspect such institutions or associate itself with
other selected educational training and research institutions, provide them
with services and facilities for the effective discharge of their functions and
responsibilities and determine teaching methodology techniques and strategies
in order to ensure the most effective educational training and research
programmes;
(vii) receive and manage
property, grants, bequests, trusts, gifts, donations, endowments and other
contributions made to the School and to invest them in such manner as it may
deem fit;
(viii) enter into agreements,
contracts and arrangements with Government, organizations, institutions, bodies
or individuals for carrying out its functions and activities;
(ix) demand and receive such fees
and other charges as it may determine
(x) appoint members of the
various bodies and committees, as the Board may determine for instructional and
co-curricular activities;
(xi) appoint such officers
including teachers and members of the staff and prescribe terms and conditions,
powers and duties of such officers and staff;
(xii) do all such other acts and
things as may be requisite to further its objectives;

8. The Chairman of the Board
of Governors.--(1) The Chairman shall be a person of eminence, known for
his contributions in the field of knowledge or service to society and
appreciated for his high moral and intellectual calibre;
(2) The Chairman shall be
appointed by the Patron on the recommendation made by the Board;
(3) The Chairman shall, when
present, preside at the convocations of the School;
(4) Every proposal to confer an
honorary degree shall be subject to confirmation by the Chairman;
(5) If the Chairman is satisfied
that the proceedings of any Authority or orders of any officer are not in
accordance with the provisions of this Act, the Statutes, the Regulations, or
the Rules, he may after calling upon such Authority or officer to show cause
why such proceedings should not be annulled, by order in writing annul such
proceedings or orders.
(6) Should the Chairman be
incapacitated from acting as such due to absence or any other cause, the
Chairman of the Executive Committee shall act for him.

CHAPTER II
OFFICERS OF THE
SCHOOL
11. Executive Director.-
(1) The Executive Director shall be appointed by the Board on the
recommendation of the Executive Committee;
(2) The Executive Director.--At
any time when the office of the Executive Director is vacant or the Executive
Director is absent or is unable to perform the functions of his officer due to
any cause, the Chairman of the. Executive Committee shall make such arrangement
for the performance of the duties of the Executive Director as he may deem fit;
(3) The Executive Director shall
be the principal academic and administrative officer of the School, and shall
be responsible for proper implementation of the provisions of this Act,
directions to the Board, decisions of the Executive Committee and execution of
the policies and programmes of the School assigned by the Executive Committee;
(4) The Executive Director may in
an emergency which in his opinion require immediate action, take such action as
he may deem necessary and shall, thereafter as soon as possible, report his
action to an officer authority or other body, which in the ordinary course
would have dealt with the matter;
(5) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, the Executive Director
shall also have the following powers--
(a) to sanction all expenditure
provided for in the approved budget and to re-appropriate funds within the same
major head of expenditure;
(b) to direct teachers, officers
and other employees of the School to take up such assignments in connection
with teaching, research, examination, administration and such other activities
in the School, as he may consider necessary;
(c) to delegate subject to such
conditions if any, as may be prescribed, any of his Powers under this Act to an
officer or other employee of the School;
(d) to appoint employees of such
categories in respect of which powers have been delegated to him by the Board;
(e) to exercise and perform such
other powers and functions as may be delegated to him by the Executive
Committee from time to time;

CHAPTER III
AUTHORITIES OF THE
SCHOOL
13. Board of Governors.--(1)
The general supervision and control of the affairs of the School and its power
to lay down policies shall vest in the Board consisting of the following--
(a) the
Chairman;
(b) the Chief
Justice of the High Court of Sindh or a Judge of the High Court to be nominated
by him;
(c) the
Secretary to the Government of Sindh Education Department;
(d) the
Chairman, University Grants Commission, or whole time Member of the Commission
to be nominated by him;
(e) All the
members of the Board of Governors of the Society nominated by the Chairman;
(2) A member nominated by the
Chief Justice of the High Court of Sindh under clause (b) or by the Chairman of
the University Grants Commission under clause (d) or by the Chairman under
clause (e) shall hold office for a term of three years unless he earlier ceases
to be a member by resignation or the nomination of another person in his place
by the authority nominating him;
(3) The Executive Director shall
act as the Secretary of the Board;
(4) No act or proceedings of the
Board shall be invalid by reason only of the existence of a vacancy in or a
defect in the constitution of the Board;
(5) A casual vacancy of a
nominated member shall be filled by the authority which had nominated the
member whose vacancy is to be filled.;

14. Powers and Functions of
the Board.--(1) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of
the provisions of subsection (1) of section 13, the Board shall exercise and
perform the powers and functions as follows--
(a) to hold, control and
administer the property, funds assets and resources of the School;
(b) to transfer and accept
transfer of movable or immovable property on behalf of the School;
(c) to affiliate and disaffiliate
educational institutions;
(d) to consider and approve, on
the advice of the Executive Committee, the annual and revised budget estimates
and to lay down guidelines or rules of business dealing with financial matters;
(e) to approve, carry out, vary
or cancel contracts on behalf of the School;
(f) to initiate and approve
schemes for achievement of the objectives of the School;
(g) to determine the form, and
regulate the custody and use of common seal of the School;
(h) to create professional, research,
administrative posts and such other posts as may be required to carry out the
purposes of the School, suspend or abolish such post;
(i) to appoint the Executive
Director and the Registrar on the recommendation of the Executive Committee;
(j) to suspend, punish and remove
from service the School employees whom it is empowered to appoint, in the
manner prescribed after due enquiry and defence;
(k) to approve regulations or
rules on the recommendations of the Executive Committee, and;
(1) to determine, regulate and
administer all other matters concerning the School and; to this end, exercise
all necessary powers not specifically mentioned in this Act or, the statutes,
the regulations or the rules;
(2) The Board may delegate any of
its powers to an authority or officer or a committee or a sub-committee

15. Meetings of the Board.--(1)
The Board shall meet at least twice in a year on the dates to be fixed by the
Chairman;
Provided that a special meeting
may be called at any time by the Chairman or on a requisition made by the
Executive Committee or by not less than four members of the Board to consider a
matter of urgent nature;
(2) Not less than ten clear day's
notice of a special meeting shall be given to the members of the Board, and the
agenda of the meeting shall be restricted to the matter for which the special
meeting is called;
(3) The quorum for a meeting of
the Board shall be one-third of its members, a fraction being counted as one.
(4) The decision of the Board
shall be expressed in terms of the views of the majority of the members present
and voting and, it the members are equally divided, the Chairman shall have and
exercise a casting vote;

The Executive Committee

ACT XVI OF 1994

and assented to by the Governor of Sindh on 13th July, 1994 is hereby published

CHAPTER III
AUTHORITIES OF THE
SCHOOL
16. The Executive Committee.--(1)
Subject to the provisions of this Act, the statutes, the regulations or the
rules and the general or special directions of the Board the Executive Committee
shall be responsible for the administration of the School and execution of
policies and directions of the Board for carrying out the purpose of this Act.
(2) The Executive Committee shall
exercise such powers as may be delegated to it by the Board from time to time;
(3) The Executive Committee shall
consist of--
(a) The Chairman
as appointed under section 10 (1);
(b) One member
of the Board nominated by the Board;
(c) The
Executive Director;
(d) Three
persons nominated by the Board from amongst the members of the Society;
(e) Three
persons co-opted by the members listed under clauses (a) to
(d) above from
amongst the members of the Society at least one of whom shall be an architect
and one shall be an artist/designer;
(4) A member nominated or co-opted
under clause (d) or (e) shall hold office for a term of three years and shall
be eligible for renomination or co option as the case may be unless he earlier
ceases to be a member by resignation or fails to attend three consecutive
meetings of the Executive Committee without sufficient cause or leave of
absence, or another person is nominated or co-opted in his place by the
authority which originally nominated or co-opted him;
(5) The Executive Committee shall
meet at least once every two months on dates to be fixed by its Chairman,
provided that a special meeting may be called, at any time on a requisition
made by not less than three members of the Executive Committee to consider a
matter of urgent nature;
(6) Any such requisition must
state the object of the meeting proposed to be called, and the Chairman of the
Executive Committee shall forthwith but not later than seven days call a
meeting of the Executive Committee, and the agenda of the meeting shall be
restricted to the matter for which the special meeting is called;
(7) The quorum for a meeting of
the Executive Committee shall be one half of the total number of members a
fraction being counted as one;
(8) The Registrar shall act as
the Secretary of the Executive Committee;

Academic Committee

CHAPTER III
AUTHORITIES OF THE
SCHOOL
17. Academic Committee.--(1)
The Academic Committee shall be the highest academic body of the School, and
shall, subject to the provisions of this Act and the statutes, have the power
to lay down proper standards of instructions, research and examination, and to
regulate and promote the academic life of the School;
(2) In particular and without
prejudice of the generality of the foregoing provisions, the Academic Committee
shall have the powers--
(a) to advise
the Executive Committee on academic matters;
(b) to regulate
the admission of students to the courses of studies and examination;
(c) to propose
to the Executive Committee schemes for the constitution and organization of
Faculties, Teaching Department Institutes and Board of Studies;
(d) to consider
or formulate proposals for the planning and development of teaching and
research in the School;
(e) to prescribe
the courses of studies and the syllabi for all teaching departments;
(t) to recognize
the examinations of other schools, colleges, and Universities or examining
bodies as equivalent to the corresponding examinations of the School;
(g) to frame
regulations for submission to the Executive Committee;
(h) to perform
such other functions as may be assigned to it by the Executive Committee;
(3) The Academic Committee shall
consist of--
(a) The
Executive Director, who shall be the Chairman;
(b) the Deans;
(c) the Chairman
of the Teaching Departments;
(d) four persons
of eminence to be nominated by the Executive. Committee at least one of whom
shall be an architect, one of whom shall be an artist and one of whom shall be
a designer;
(4) A nominated member shall hold
office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for renomination, unless
his nomination is changed by the authority which nominated him;
(5) The office of a nominated
member, shall become vacant if he resigns or fails to attend three consecutive
meetings of the Academic Committee without sufficient cause or leave or
absence;
(6) The quorum for a meeting of
the Academic Committee shall be one? half of the total number of members, a
fraction being counted as one;
(7) The Executive Director shall
nominate a Chairman of a Teaching Department to act as the Secretary of the
Academic Committee;

18 The Finance and Planning
Committee.--(1) The functions of the Finance and Planning Committee shall
be;
(a) to consider
annual statement of accounts and annual and revised budget estimates and advise
the Executive Committee thereon;
(b) to review
periodically the financial position of the School;
(c) to. advise
the Executive Committee on all matters relating to planning, develpment,
finance, investment and accounts of the School;
(d) to prepare
short term and long term development plans;
(e) to prepare
staff and resources development plans, and; .
(f) to perform
such other functions as may be prescribed by the statutes, or assigned to it by
the Executive Committee;
(2) The Finance and Planning
Committee shall consist of--
(a) The Chairman
nominated by the Board from amongst its members;
(b) Two members of the Executive Committee
nominated by the Executive Committee;
(c) The
Executive Director;
(d) The Deans;
(e) A professional
Chartered Accountant or a professional banker nominated by the Executive
Committee;
(3) A member nominated under
clause (b) shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible
for re nomination unless he earlier resigns or fails to attend three
consecutive meetings of the Finance and Planning Committee without sufficient
cause of leave or absence or has ceased to be member of the Board or the
Executive Committee as the case may be;
(4) The member nominated under
clause (e) shall hold office for a term of three years unless he earlier
resigns or his nomination is changed by the Executive Committee;
(5) The quorum for a meeting of
the Finance and Planning Committee shall be one-half of the total number of
members, a fraction being counted as one.
(6) The Registrar shall act as
Secretary of the Finance and Planning Committee;

21. Statutes.--(1) Subject
to the provisions, of this Act, statutes may be statutes made to regulate or
prescribe all or any of the following matters namely--
(a) terms and
conditions of service of employees of the School including scales of pay,
constitution of pension insurance, gratuity, provident fund, benevolent fund
and other fringe benefits.
(b) terms and
conditions of contractual appointments of teachers researchers and officers;.
(c)
establishment of Faculties, Teaching Departments and other academic units and
divisions;
(d) powers and
duties of officers and teachers;
(e) conditions
under which the School may enter into arrangements with other public or private
organizations for purposes of instruction, research and other scholarly
activities;
(f) efficiency
and discipline of the employees of the School;
(g) acquisition
and administration of properties and investments of the Schools, and;
(h) all other
matters which under this Act are required to be or may be prescribed or
regulated by statutes;
(2) The draft of the Statutes
shall be proposed by the Executive Committee for approval by the Board;
(3) The Board shall have the
powers to give assent to the statutes submitted to it for approval or refer
them back to the Executive Committee for reconsideration;
(4) No statute shall be valid
until it has been approved by the Board and signed by the Chairman;

CHAPTER V
THE SCHOOL FUND
24. The School fund audit and
accounts.--(1) The School shall have a fund to which shall be credited its
income from fees, donations, trusts, bequests, endowments, grants,
contributions and all other such sources.
(2) Capital and recurrent
expenditure of the School be met other foundations, universities and
individuals, and from the income from the contributions made by the Society and
any other source, including derived from, such sources.
(3) No contribution, donation or
grant which may directly or indirectly involve any immediate or subsequent
financial liability for the School; or which may involve an activity not
included in the programmes for the time being, shall be accepted without prior approval
of the Executive Committee.
(4) The accounts of the School
shall be maintained in such form and manner as may be determined by the Board
and shall be audited each year within four months of the closing of the
financial year of the School by the Chartered Accountant appointed by the
Board.
(5) The account, together with
the report of the auditor thereon shall be submitted to the Board for approval;

the Board.--(1) Where an order is passed punishing an employee of the

teacher of the school have the right to appeal to the Board, against the order,

nominated members of any Authority shall be filled as soon as conveniently may
be, by the person or the body who appointed or nominated the member whose place
has become vacant, and the person appointed or nominated to the vacancy shall
be a member of such Authority for the residue of the term for which the person
whose place he fills would have been a member:

the organization, institution or other body, other than the School has ceased
to exist or has ceased to function, or for any other circumstances which make
it impracticable to fill the vacancy, the vacancy shall be filled in such
manner as the Chairman may direct on the recommendation of the Board.
